name: Do I need a permit to relocate bathroom plumbing in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit to relocate bathroom plumbing in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Do I need a permit to relocate bathroom plumbing in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, bathroom plumbing relocation in Los Angeles typically requires a permit when the work changes drain lines, venting, or fixture locations. Simple fixture swaps may be different from full reroutes, but once pipes are being moved, inspected plumbing work is usually part of the process. This matters because the new layout has to pass inspection before the walls, slab, or tile are closed. Permitting also helps protect the remodel schedule by making sure rough-in work is documented before finish materials are installed. Homeowners should ask whether the contractor is handling permit submission, inspection scheduling, and any correction notes from the city. In dense remodel areas, permit timing can affect project duration, so it should be discussed before demolition starts. A good estimate should clarify exactly what plumbing changes are included and whether permit fees, engineering, or plan revisions are separate.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, plumbing relocation for a bathroom remodel typically requires a permit when drains, vents, or fixture locations are changed. The work is usually inspected before walls, floors, or concrete are closed up, especially for toilet, shower, and drain reroutes.
